newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius rupee strengthens on dollar and pound.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius rupee strengthens on dollar and pound.

text.p: The Mauritian rupee strengthened against both the dollar and pound on Tuesday, reflecting international trends, commercial dealers said.
The rupee was posted at a mean commercial rate of 20.662 for one dollar from 20.692 on Monday. Against the pound, the rupee firmed to a mean rate of 32.2895 from Monday's 32.3790.

Dealers said the rupee's fixing against the dollar reflected the American currency's trend in overnight international markets despite weakening pressure on the local currency, arising from a slight shortage in commercial banks reserves.
"The central bank intervened by selling dollars in the interbank forex market on Monday mid-afternoon and this brought relief to the shortage situation which existed in banks," one dealer said.
The dealer added that the central bank's Monday intervention rate was close to the prevailing interbank rate.
Last week commercial banks rapidly ran short in hard currency owing to higher demand from importers entering in forward contracts.
Dealers said the level of demand was not satisfied despite receipts from the island's current high tourism season. Tourism is the third largest foreign exchange earner for Mauritius.
